newsitem.title: FRANCE: Veteran film stars piqued at non-invite to Cannes.
newsitem.headline: Veteran film stars piqued at non-invite to Cannes.

text.p: Jean-Paul Belmondo and Alain Delon, once the biggest box office draws in French film, have jointly complained they were not invited to the annual Cannes film festival which opened on Wednesday.
"For this festival of the French cinema industry, they invited (buxom American star) Pamela Anderson and not us. Soemthing is rotten somewhere," Delon told the weekly Paris-Match.
The two actors, now in their early 60s, made dozens of highly successful films from the late 1950s until about a decade ago.

Their hits included dramatic classics, like Delon in the Italian film "Rocco and his Brothers," comedies like "That Man from Rio" with Belmondo or thrillers like "Borsalino" in which the two acted together.
But virtually all their recent movies have been flops, possibly because their once youthful charm and good looks have faded.

Belmondo, who still draws crowds for his frequent stage appearances, has several times accused French film distributors of being more interested in launching Hollywood blockbusters than in backing locally-made films.
"I've already said our film industry was down on its knees before Hollywood. This is just a new proof of this," Belmondo told the magazine Paris-Match.
